title: Gepirone
overview: Gepirone has been discontinued in the US. Because this drug is no longer available in the US market, the material in this monograph is no longer updated by ASHP PMI. If this drug is used in countries other than the U.S., it is essential that the manufacturers’ labeling be consulted for more recently available information.

sections.Before taking gepirone,: tell your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to gepirone, any other medications, or any of the ingredients in gepirone tablets. Ask your pharmacist or check the Medication Guide for a list of the ingredients.Some medications should not be taken with gepirone. Other medications may cause dosing changes or extra monitoring when taken with gepirone. Make sure you have discussed any medications you are currently taking or plan to take before starting gepirone with your doctor and pharmacist. Before starting, stopping, or changing any medications while taking gepirone, please get the advice of your doctor or pharmacist.tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking the following medications or have stopped taking them within the past two weeks: monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors such as isocarboxazid (Marplan®), linezolid (Zyvox®), methylene blue, phenelzine (Nardil®), rasagiline (Azilect), selegiline (Emsam®, Zelapar®), and tranylcypromine (Parnate®).The following nonprescription or herbal products may interact with gepirone: St. John's wort. Be sure to let your doctor and pharmacist know that you are taking this medication before you start taking gepirone. Do not start this medication while taking gepirone without discussing with your healthcare provider.tell your doctor if you or anyone in your family has or has ever had a prolonged QT interval (a rare heart problem that may cause irregular heartbeat, fainting, or sudden death) or liver problems. Your doctor may tell you not to take gepirone.tell your doctor if you have recently had a heart attack and if you have or have ever had a slow or irregular heartbeat, heart failure, or any other heart problems; high blood pressure; a low level of potassium, magnesium, or sodium in your blood; or kidney disease.tell your doctor if you are pregnant, especially if you are in the last few months of your pregnancy, or if you plan to become pregnant or are breast-feeding. If you become pregnant while taking gepirone, call your doctor. Gepirone may cause problems in newborns following delivery if it is taken during the last months of pregnancy.

sections.Some side effects can be serious. If you: seizuresfever, sweating, confusion, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe muscle stiffness or twitching, agitation, hallucinations, loss of coordination, nausea, vomiting, or diarrheaseizuresGepirone may cause other side effects. Call your doctor if you have any unusual problems while taking this medication.If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online (https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).
